title: Four Square
summary: A playground ball game in which four players each stand in their own painted square and bounce a rubber ball into another player's square with the hand. Whoever cannot return it fairly drops out and the others move up a square. Here you practise the serve: bounce the ball into the far squares for more points.
howToPlay: Press at the ball, then pull back to set the direction and the strength.
Release to bounce the ball: the dotted line shows where it will land.
Each of the four painted squares has its own number; the far squares are worth more.
Six bounces make a round. Land them in the high squares to earn stars.
rules: The court is a square split by a cross into four equal boxes numbered 1 to 4; the two far boxes are 3 and 4, with 4 the "king" square in the real game.
A bounce scores the number of the square where the ball comes to rest.
A ball that stops outside the squares, or leaves the court, scores nothing.
Six bounces make a round; all six are added up.
Three stars are awarded at 8, 14 and 19 points.
heritageNote: Four square is a schoolyard game from the United States, played on asphalt with a painted court and a rubber ball. Local rules for serving, faults and names for the squares differ from school to school and are handed down among children.
